question: As per the Census data, What was the density of population in India in 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 382 persons/sq km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, the population density of India was 382 persons per sq km, up from 325 persons per sq km in 2001. (जनसंख्या घनत्व — 382 व्यक्ति प्रति वर्ग किमी)

 

• Population density is defined as the number of persons living per unit area (per sq km) of a region.

 

• India's total population as per the 2011 Census was 121.09 crore (1,210.9 million), spread over a geographical area of about 32.87 lakh sq km.

 

• Bihar recorded the highest population density among states (1,102 persons/sq km) while Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest (17 persons/sq km); among UTs, Delhi had the highest density.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years; the first synchronous census was in 1881 and the most recent completed one was in 2011.

 

• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after Independence, with the theme "Our Census, Our Future".

 

NOTE

 

• 822, 328 and 282 persons/sq km (Options 1, 3, 4): These figures do not match the actual 2011 Census density of 382 persons/sq km and are incorrect distractors.

question: Who among the following was the Maharana of Mewar and composed a book on music called ‘Sangeet Raj’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharana Kumbha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Maharana Kumbha (Rana Kumbha) was the ruler of Mewar (r. 1433-1468 CE) and a great scholar-king who composed the treatise on music titled ‘Sangeet Raj’. (महाराणा कुंभा — संगीत राज)

 

• He was also the author of other works including ‘Sangeet Mimansa’, ‘Sangeet Ratnakar’ (commentary) and ‘Rasik Priya’ (a commentary on Jayadeva's Gita Govinda).

 

• Maharana Kumbha was a great builder as well; he constructed the famous Kirti Stambh (Tower of Fame) at Chittorgarh and several forts including Kumbhalgarh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vijay Stambh (Tower of Victory) at Chittorgarh was built by Maharana Kumbha to commemorate his victory over Mahmud Khilji of Malwa.

 

• Kumbhalgarh Fort, built by Maharana Kumbha, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan) and has the second-longest continuous wall in the world after the Great Wall of China.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharana Sanga (Option 1): Rana Sangram Singh (Rana Sanga) was a Mewar ruler famous for fighting Babur at the Battle of Khanwa (1527); he is not credited with 'Sangeet Raj'.

 

• Maharana Pratap (Option 2): He is celebrated for resisting Akbar and fighting the Battle of Haldighati (1576), not for composing musical treatises.

 

• Maharana Udai Singh (Option 4): He founded the city of Udaipur in 1559; he is not associated with 'Sangeet Raj'.

question: How many silver medals was won by India in Tokyo Paralympic 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won a record 19 medals at the Tokyo Paralympics 2020 (held in 2021): 5 gold, 8 silver and 6 bronze. (टोक्यो पैरालंपिक 2020 — भारत के 8 रजत पदक)

 

• This was India's best-ever performance at the Paralympic Games, finishing 24th in the medal tally.

 

• Notable gold medallists included Avani Lekhara (shooting, India's first woman to win a Paralympic gold), Sumit Antil, Krishna Nagar, Pramod Bhagat and Manish Narwal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Avani Lekhara won gold in the 10m Air Rifle Standing SH1 event and bronze in the 50m Rifle 3 Positions SH1 event.

 

• The Tokyo 2020 Paralympics were held from 24 August to 5 September 2021 (postponed from 2020 due to COVID-19).

 

NOTE

 

• 7, 6 and 5 (Options 1, 2, 4): These figures do not match India's actual silver medal count of 8 at Tokyo 2020 Paralympics and are incorrect distractors.

question:
Match the columns.

Column-A (Common name)          Column-B (Group number in the Modern Periodic Table)

i. Alkali metals          a. 18

ii. Alkaline earth metals          b. 17

iii. Halogens          c. 2

iv. Noble gases          d. 1
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Modern Periodic Table, elements are arranged into 18 groups, and each group listed here corresponds correctly as: Alkali metals - Group 1, Alkaline earth metals - Group 2, Halogens - Group 17, Noble gases - Group 18. (आधुनिक आवर्त सारणी — समूह क्रमांक)

 

• Alkali metals (Group 1): Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr - soft, highly reactive metals with one valence electron.

 

• Alkaline earth metals (Group 2): Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, Ra - have two valence electrons, less reactive than alkali metals.

 

• Halogens (Group 17): F, Cl, Br, I, At - highly reactive non-metals with seven valence electrons.

 

• Noble gases (Group 18): He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn - have completely filled outer shells, making them chemically inert.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Modern Periodic Table is based on Henry Moseley's Law, arranging elements by increasing atomic number.

 

• Groups 3-12 constitute the transition metals, positioned between the alkaline earth metals and the boron group.

 

NOTE

 

• i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d (Option 1): Incorrectly assigns Group 18 to alkali metals, Group 17 to alkaline earth metals, Group 2 to halogens and Group 1 to noble gases.

 

• i-a, ii-c, iii-b, iv-d (Option 2): Incorrectly assigns Group 18 to alkali metals and Group 1 to noble gases.

 

• i-b, ii-a, iii-c, iv-d (Option 3): Incorrectly assigns Group 17 to alkali metals, Group 18 to alkaline earth metals and Group 1 to noble gases.

question: Pectin, which is responsible for the firmness and softness of fruits, is mainly composed of which acid unit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Galacturonic acid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pectin is a complex polysaccharide (heteropolysaccharide) found in the cell walls of plants, mainly composed of chains of galacturonic acid units. (पेक्टिन — गैलेक्टुरोनिक अम्ल)

 

• Pectin is responsible for the firmness, texture and softening behaviour of fruits as they ripen, and is widely used as a gelling agent in jams and jellies.

 

• It is particularly abundant in the peels of citrus fruits and apples, and is extracted commercially from these sources.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pectin is a type of dietary fibre and is used in the food industry as a thickening, stabilising and gelling agent.

 

• During fruit ripening, enzymes like pectinase break down pectin, causing the fruit to soften.

 

NOTE

 

• Aspartic acid (Option 1): A non-essential amino acid, a building block of proteins, not related to pectin.

 

• Lactic acid (Option 3): An organic acid produced during anaerobic respiration/fermentation, unrelated to pectin structure.

 

• Glutamic acid (Option 4): A non-essential amino acid, a component of proteins (and the source of the flavour compound MSG), not related to pectin.

question: Sporophyte stage is dominant in which plant group?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vascular plants.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plants show an alternation of generations between a haploid gametophyte and a diploid sporophyte stage; in vascular plants, the sporophyte generation is the dominant, independent phase. (बीजाणुद्भिद प्रभावी अवस्था — संवहनी पादप)

 

• Vascular plants (Tracheophytes) include pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms - in all of these, the sporophyte is the larger, longer-lived, photosynthetic plant body, while the gametophyte is reduced.

 

• This is in contrast to bryophytes, where the gametophyte is the dominant stage and the sporophyte remains attached to and dependent on it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• In angiosperms and gymnosperms, the gametophyte is extremely reduced (e.g., the pollen grain and embryo sac) and is retained within the sporophyte tissue.

 

• Bryophytes include mosses, liverworts and hornworts - simple, non-vascular plants.

 

NOTE

 

• Bryophytes (Option 1): Here the gametophyte, not the sporophyte, is the dominant, free-living stage.

 

• Algae (Option 3): Life cycles vary widely among algae; there is no single dominant sporophyte-generation rule as in vascular plants, and many algae are gametophyte-dominant or show no clear sporophyte dominance.

 

• Pteridophytes (Option 4): While sporophyte is also dominant here, pteridophytes are only a subset of the broader, more complete answer 'Vascular plants', which also includes gymnosperms and angiosperms.

question: The country can improve its balance of payments by devaluation when the sum of elasticity of demand for exports and imports is ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is greater than unity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This is described by the Marshall-Lerner Condition, which states that a devaluation of currency will improve a country's balance of payments only if the sum of the price elasticities of demand for exports and imports (in absolute terms) is greater than one (unity). (मार्शल-लर्नर शर्त — एकता से अधिक)

 

• Devaluation is a deliberate downward adjustment of a country's currency value relative to another currency, group of currencies, or a standard, under a fixed exchange rate regime.

 

• If the sum of elasticities is less than unity, devaluation would actually worsen the balance of payments instead of improving it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Marshall-Lerner condition is named after economists Alfred Marshall and Abba P. Lerner.

 

• The J-curve effect describes the short-run worsening followed by long-run improvement of the trade balance after a devaluation, as elasticities tend to be low in the short run and higher in the long run.

 

NOTE

 

• Less than unity (Option 1): Under this condition, devaluation would worsen, not improve, the balance of payments.

 

• Equal to unity (Option 2): In this case, devaluation would leave the balance of payments unchanged in value terms.

 

• Zero (Option 4): This implies perfectly inelastic demand, in which case devaluation would only worsen the trade balance in value terms.

question: __________ became India’s first sports unicorn with its market cap having touched a high of Rs.7,600 crores as of 30 January 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chennai Super Kings.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chennai Super Kings Cricket Limited (CSKCL), the entity owning IPL franchise Chennai Super Kings, became India's first sports unicorn, with its market capitalisation touching a high of Rs. 7,600 crore (about $1 billion) as of 30 January 2022. (चेन्नई सुपर किंग्स — भारत का पहला स्पोर्ट्स यूनिकॉर्न)

 

• CSK is owned by India Cements Group, led by N. Srinivasan, and is captained by MS Dhoni.

 

• A 'unicorn' refers to a privately-held company/enterprise valued at over $1 billion; CSK became the first sporting entity from India to attain this valuation.

 

• CSKCL shares are listed and traded on the BSE's SME platform.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• MS Dhoni has led CSK to five IPL titles (2010, 2011, 2018, 2021, 2023).

 

• CSK's home ground is the MA Chidambaram Stadium, Chepauk, Chennai.

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi Capitals, Kolkata Knight Riders, Mumbai Indians (Options 1, 2, 3): These are other IPL franchises, but none of them achieved unicorn status as CSK did in January 2022.

question: Which of the following committees was constituted to study the issues and concerns in the Micro Finance Institution in 2010?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Malegam Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The RBI constituted the Malegam Committee in 2010, headed by Y. H. Malegam, to study the issues and concerns in the Microfinance Institutions (MFI) sector, following the Andhra Pradesh MFI crisis. (मालेगाम समिति — सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थान)

 

• The committee submitted its report in January 2011, recommending the creation of a separate category of NBFCs called NBFC-MFIs, along with a cap on interest rates and margins.

 

• Its recommendations led to a comprehensive regulatory framework for MFIs by the RBI.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Y. H. Malegam also headed other RBI committees, including one on disclosure norms for banks' financial statements.

 

• The NBFC-MFI category created after this report is regulated separately with a specified capital adequacy ratio and lending norms.

 

NOTE

 

• Ghosh Committee (Option 1): Related to frauds and malpractices in banks (1992).

 

• Sivaraman Committee (Option 2): Recommended the establishment of NABARD (1979).

 

• Khan Committee (Option 4): Related to financial inclusion and business correspondent/banking correspondent model (2005).

question: India borrowed the DPSP from the _______ Constitution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Irish.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), given in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution, were borrowed from the Irish Constitution (1937). (नीति निदेशक तत्व — आयरलैंड का संविधान)

 

• The concept of DPSP itself was inspired by the Irish Free State, which had in turn borrowed the idea from the Spanish Constitution.

 

• DPSP are aimed at establishing social and economic democracy in India and are non-justiciable, i.e., not enforceable by courts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called the DPSP the 'novel features' of the Indian Constitution.

 

• India also borrowed features like single citizenship, the method of election of the President, and the concept of nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha from the Irish Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Australian Constitution (Option 1): India borrowed concepts like Concurrent List, freedom of trade and commerce, and joint sitting of Parliament from Australia.

 

• German Constitution (Option 3): India borrowed the provision of suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency from the Weimar Constitution of Germany.

 

• Austrian Constitution (Option 4): India did not borrow the DPSP or any major distinctive feature from the Austrian Constitution.

question: Tamladu is a festival celebrated by the Buddhist community of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tamladu (Tamla Du) is a major festival celebrated by the Idu Mishmi community of Arunachal Pradesh, dedicated to the worship of Mother Earth (Nanyi Intaya) and the Fire God. (तमलाडू महोत्सव — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

 

• It is celebrated every year on the 1st or 15th of February and involves prayers for a good harvest, prosperity and the wellbeing of the community and its livestock.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh, in the far northeastern Himalayas, is home to numerous tribal communities with distinct festivals, including the Idu Mishmi, Adi, Nyishi and Apatani.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of Arunachal Pradesh include Losar (Monpa tribe, Buddhist New Year), Solung (Adi tribe) and Nyokum (Nyishi tribe).

 

• The capital of Arunachal Pradesh is Itanagar; it shares borders with Bhutan, Tibet (China) and Myanmar.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Not associated with the Tamladu festival; known for festivals like Ugadi and Karaga.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Not associated with Tamladu; known for festivals like Bhagoria.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 4): Not associated with Tamladu; known for festivals like Kullu Dussehra.

question: Iron mines in Jharkhand attributed to the rise of which of the following kingdoms in ancient India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magadha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The rise of the Magadha kingdom (in present-day Bihar/Jharkhand region) as the most powerful state of ancient India is attributed to easy access to iron ore deposits in the Jharkhand region (Chota Nagpur plateau). (मगध साम्राज्य — झारखंड के लौह अयस्क)

 

• Access to iron ore allowed Magadha to manufacture superior weapons and agricultural tools, giving it a military and economic edge over rival kingdoms.

 

• Magadha's fertile Gangetic plains, control over trade routes, and access to elephants also contributed to its dominance, eventually leading to the rise of empires like the Mauryas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Magadha's early capital was Rajgir (Girivraja), later shifted to Pataliputra under the Nandas and Mauryas.

 

• Notable Magadhan dynasties include the Haryanka, Shishunaga, Nanda, Mauryan, Shunga and Gupta dynasties.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuru (Option 1): An early Vedic-age kingdom centred around modern Delhi/Haryana, associated with the Kuru-Panchala culture, not the Jharkhand iron mines.

 

• Kashi (Option 3): One of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, centred around modern Varanasi, known for trade and textiles rather than iron resources.

 

• Kushan (Option 4): A later empire (1st-3rd century CE) originating from Central Asia, ruling over northwestern India, unrelated to Jharkhand's iron mines.

question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about granite?
option_1: Granite is the most abundant rock in the continental crust.
option_2: It is the most common sedimentary rock.
option_3: These are igneous rocks that form when hot, molten rock crystallises and solidifies.
option_4: Granite is composed mainly of quartz and feldspar with minor amounts of mica.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is the most common sedimentary rock..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Granite is an igneous rock, not a sedimentary rock, so the statement calling it 'the most common sedimentary rock' is INCORRECT. (ग्रेनाइट — आग्नेय शैल, अवसादी नहीं)

 

• Granite is a coarse-grained, intrusive (plutonic) igneous rock that forms from the slow crystallisation and solidification of molten magma beneath the Earth's surface.

 

• It is the most abundant rock in the Earth's continental crust and is mainly composed of quartz, feldspar, with minor amounts of mica and other minerals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common sedimentary rocks include sandstone, limestone and shale, formed by the compaction and cementation of sediments.

 

• Other well-known igneous rocks include basalt (extrusive) and gabbro (intrusive).

 

NOTE

 

• Granite is the most abundant rock in the continental crust (Option 1): This is a correct statement about granite.

 

• These are igneous rocks that form when hot, molten rock crystallises and solidifies (Option 3): This is a correct statement about granite.

 

• Granite is composed mainly of quartz and feldspar with minor amounts of mica (Option 4): This is a correct statement about granite's composition.

question: ‘Luddi’ is a folk dance of which of the following states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Luddi is a popular folk dance of Punjab, traditionally performed by men to celebrate victory or joyous occasions, often accompanied by the dhol. (लुड्डी नृत्य — पंजाब)

 

• It is typically performed with slow, graceful movements of the arms and body, in contrast to the more energetic Bhangra.

 

• Punjab's rich folk dance tradition also includes Bhangra (men) and Giddha (women), both associated with harvest and festive celebrations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhangra, originally linked to the harvest festival of Baisakhi, is the most globally recognised folk dance of Punjab.

 

• Giddha is a popular folk dance performed by women of Punjab, often incorporating verses called bolis.

 

NOTE

 

• Manipur (Option 1): Known for classical Manipuri dance and folk forms like the Thang-Ta martial dance.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Known for folk dances like Karma and Saila.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Known for classical dance forms like Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

question: Commonwealth Games 2022 was held in _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birmingham.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 Commonwealth Games, officially the XXII Commonwealth Games, were held in Birmingham, England, from 28 July to 8 August 2022. (राष्ट्रमंडल खेल 2022 — बर्मिंघम)

 

• India finished 4th in the medal tally with 61 medals (22 gold, 16 silver, 23 bronze).

 

• These were the first Commonwealth Games to feature more women's medal events than men's, reflecting a push toward gender equity in sport.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The next (2026) Commonwealth Games are scheduled to be held in Glasgow, Scotland.

 

• The 2018 Commonwealth Games were held in the Gold Coast, Australia.

 

NOTE

 

• Beijing (Option 2): Hosted the 2008 and 2022 Olympic Games (summer and winter), not the Commonwealth Games.

 

• Tokyo (Option 3): Hosted the 2020 (held in 2021) Summer Olympics and Paralympics, not the Commonwealth Games.

 

• New Delhi (Option 4): Hosted the 2010 Commonwealth Games, not the 2022 edition.

question: ‘Back to Vedas’ was the slogan of which Reform Movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Arya Samaj, founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 in Bombay, gave the famous slogan 'Back to the Vedas', calling for a return to the pure, original teachings of the Vedas. (आर्य समाज — वेदों की ओर लौटो)

 

• Swami Dayanand Saraswati authored the book 'Satyarth Prakash', which laid out the core philosophy of the Arya Samaj.

 

• The Arya Samaj rejected idol worship, caste rigidity and untouchability, and promoted the Shuddhi movement (reconversion to Hinduism) along with the establishment of DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) schools.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arya Samaj headquarters, Kendriya Sabha, is located in New Delhi.

 

• The movement significantly influenced the growth of nationalism, especially in Punjab.

 

NOTE

 

• Dev Samaj (Option 1): Founded by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri in 1887 in Lahore, focused on ethical and social reform.

 

• Brahmo Samaj (Option 2): Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828, it worked against sati, idol worship and caste rigidity.

 

• Prarthana Samaj (Option 3): Founded by Atmaram Pandurang in 1867 in Bombay, inspired by Brahmo Samaj ideals, and later led by M. G. Ranade.

question:
Which among the following statements about judicial review in India are correct?

A. Judicial review means that the courts of law have the power of testing the validity of legislative as well as other governmental action with reference to the provisions of the Constitution.

B. Under Article 23 of the Indian Constitution, the compulsion of judicial review was described in the Fundamental Rights in Part III.

C. The power of judicial review is significantly vested upon the High Courts and the Supreme Court of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A and C only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement A is correct: Judicial review is the power of the courts to examine the constitutionality/validity of legislative enactments and executive orders. (न्यायिक पुनरावलोकन — भारत का संविधान)

 

• Statement B is incorrect: Judicial review is rooted in Articles 13, 32 and 226, not Article 23 (which deals with the prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour, a Fundamental Right unrelated to judicial review).

 

• Statement C is correct: The power of judicial review is vested in the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the High Courts (Article 226).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 13 declares that any law inconsistent with or in derogation of the Fundamental Rights shall be void, forming the constitutional basis of judicial review.

 

• The doctrine of judicial review in India was borrowed from the Constitution of the United States of America.

 

NOTE

 

• A and B only (Option 1): Incorrectly includes Statement B, which wrongly cites Article 23 as the source of judicial review.

 

• B and C only (Option 2): Incorrectly includes Statement B, and excludes correct Statement A.

 

• A, B and C (Option 4): Incorrectly includes Statement B; only A and C are factually accurate.

question: The Ministry of Education (MoE) in February 2022 approved a new scheme _______ for the next five years to cover all the aspects of adult education to align with new the National Education Policy (NEP).
solution_text:
The correct answer is New India Literacy Programme.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ministry of Education approved the 'New India Literacy Programme' (NILP) in February 2022 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for 2022-27, covering all aspects of adult education aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. (न्यू इंडिया साक्षरता कार्यक्रम — वयस्क शिक्षा)

 

• The scheme covers five components: Foundational Literacy and Numeracy, Critical Life Skills, Vocational Skills, Basic Education, and Continuing Education.

 

• NILP uses online/digital modes primarily, through platforms like the DIKSHA portal and the ULLAS (Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society) mobile app.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NILP targets non-literate persons aged 15 years and above, aiming to cover 5 crore learners.

 

• The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 replaced the earlier National Policy on Education of 1986.

 

NOTE

 

• Open Education Programme (Option 1): Not the actual name of the adult education scheme approved in February 2022.

 

• ASHA (Option 2): Refers to Accredited Social Health Activists, a healthcare scheme, unrelated to adult education/literacy.

 

• New India Education Plan (Option 3): Not the actual name of the scheme; a distractor similar in wording to the correct answer.

question: According to India State of Forest Report 2019, what is the total forest cover in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 21.67%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2019, released by the Forest Survey of India (FSI), the total forest cover in India was 7,12,249 sq km, i.e., 21.67% of the country's geographical area. (भारत राज्य वन रिपोर्ट 2019 — 21.67% वन आवरण)

 

• The tree cover (separately) was 95,027 sq km (2.89%), making the combined forest and tree cover 24.56% of the total geographical area.

 

• ISFR 2019 showed an increase of 5,188 sq km in forest and tree cover compared to the ISFR 2017 assessment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhya Pradesh had the largest forest cover area, while Mizoram had the highest forest cover as a percentage of its geographical area.

 

• The ISFR is published biennially by the Forest Survey of India, headquartered in Dehradun.

 

NOTE

 

• 20.87% (Option 1): Does not match the ISFR 2019 forest cover figure.

 

• 24.67% and 23.67% (Options 3, 4): Close to but do not exactly match the combined forest and tree cover figure (24.56%) or the forest cover figure (21.67%) reported in ISFR 2019.

question: ‘Ras-Lila’ recognised as one of the classical dance forms of India belongs to which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ras-Lila, depicting the divine love of Radha and Krishna, is an integral and celebrated part of the classical Manipuri dance tradition of Manipur. (रास-लीला — मणिपुरी नृत्य)

 

• Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, characterised by graceful, fluid movements and elaborate costumes, especially the Kumil (cylindrical skirt) worn during Ras-Lila performances.

 

• Ras-Lila performances are deeply rooted in Vaishnavism, which became prominent in Manipur from the 18th century onward.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eight classical dance forms of India are Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

 

• Sattriya, another classical dance form with Vaishnavite roots, belongs to Assam.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 1): Known for the classical dance form Sattriya, not Ras-Lila/Manipuri dance.

 

• Meghalaya (Option 2): Known for folk dances like Wangala and Nongkrem, not for a classical dance form.

 

• Tripura (Option 3): Known for folk dances like Hojagiri, not for a classical dance form.

question: The Viceroy who took keen interest in the restoration and protection of historical monuments was _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Curzon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Curzon, Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905, took a keen personal interest in the restoration and protection of India's historical monuments. (लॉर्ड कर्जन — प्राचीन स्मारक संरक्षण)

 

• He enacted the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, 1904, providing a legal framework for the protection of archaeological sites and monuments across India.

 

• Curzon also strengthened the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), appointing John Marshall as its Director-General in 1902 and vastly expanding its scope and funding.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Curzon is also known for the controversial Partition of Bengal in 1905.

 

• He oversaw restoration work on monuments including the Taj Mahal.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Ellenborough (Option 1): Governor-General of India (1842-44), known for the annexation of Sindh, not monument preservation.

 

• Lord Auckland (Option 2): Governor-General (1836-42), known for the First Anglo-Afghan War, not monument preservation.

 

• Lord Lytton (Option 3): Viceroy (1876-80), known for the Vernacular Press Act and the Delhi Durbar of 1877, not monument preservation.

question: The Amara-Nayakas were ________ in Vijayanagara Empire.
solution_text:
The correct answer is military commanders.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Amara-Nayakas were military commanders/chiefs under the Vijayanagara Empire, appointed by the king and granted territories (amaram) in return for maintaining troops, horses and elephants for the state. (अमर-नायक — विजयनगर के सैन्य प्रमुख)

 

• They collected revenue from their assigned territories, retained a portion for their own use and the maintenance of their military contingents, and sent the rest to the royal treasury.

 

• This Amara-Nayaka system was a key administrative and military institution of the Vijayanagara Empire, showing some similarities to later systems like the Mughal Mansabdari and Iqta systems.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 CE by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty.

 

• Our knowledge of the Nayaka system comes largely from the accounts of foreign travellers like Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa.

 

NOTE

 

• Forced labourers, finance officers, ordinary peasants (Options 1, 2, 3): These do not accurately describe the role of Amara-Nayakas, who were military commanders/governors holding territorial and revenue rights in exchange for military service.

question: What is the colour of the flame when unsaturated hydrocarbons burn?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yellow.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes and alkynes), having a higher percentage of carbon relative to hydrogen, burn with a sooty, yellow, luminous flame due to incomplete combustion and unburnt carbon particles glowing white-hot. (असंतृप्त हाइड्रोकार्बन — पीली ज्वाला)

 

• In contrast, saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) generally burn with a clean, blue, non-sooty flame because they undergo more complete combustion.

 

• The sooty yellow flame is accompanied by the release of black smoke/soot, which can be tested using a cold plate held over the flame (soot deposit test).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common unsaturated hydrocarbons include ethylene (ethene) and acetylene (ethyne).

 

• Unsaturated hydrocarbons readily undergo addition reactions (e.g., decolourise bromine water), unlike saturated hydrocarbons.

 

NOTE

 

• Blue (Option 1): This is characteristic of the clean combustion of saturated hydrocarbons (e.g., methane, LPG), not unsaturated ones.

 

• Red and Green (Options 2, 3): These are not the characteristic flame colours associated with the combustion of hydrocarbons; green flames are typically associated with metal salts like copper or barium in flame tests.

question: The ‘Jal Kranti Abhiyan’ was launched by which government during the financial year 2015-2016?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Jal Kranti Abhiyan' was launched by the Government of India, through the Ministry of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, during the financial year 2015-16. (जल क्रांति अभियान — भारत सरकार)

 

• The scheme aimed to consolidate water conservation efforts across the country through a holistic and integrated approach, promoting the development of one model 'Jal Gram' (water village) in each district.

 

• It sought to strengthen grassroots involvement in water conservation, judicious use of water resources, and rejuvenation of water bodies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other central water conservation initiatives include 'Jal Shakti Abhiyan' (2019) and the creation of the Ministry of Jal Shakti (2019), merging the erstwhile Ministry of Water Resources and Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation.

 

• The National Water Mission is one of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC).

 

NOTE

 

• Government of Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh (Options 1, 2, 4): These are state governments; the 'Jal Kranti Abhiyan' was a central/national-level scheme launched by the Government of India, not by any individual state government.

question: Who among the following Supreme Court judges was in news in 2022 for recusing himself from hearing a plea against the ED chief’s tenure extension?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justice SK Kaul.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul (SK Kaul), a Supreme Court judge, recused himself in 2022 from hearing a plea challenging the tenure extension granted to Enforcement Directorate (ED) Director Sanjay Kumar Mishra. (न्यायमूर्ति एस.के. कौल — ईडी प्रमुख कार्यकाल विस्तार मामला)

 

• The matter was subsequently heard by a bench led by Justice B. R. Gavai, which in July 2023 held the repeated extensions of the ED Director's tenure to be illegal, though it allowed him to continue until 31 July 2023 for FATF-related reasons.

 

• The case involved challenges to the Central Vigilance Commission (Amendment) Act, 2021, which enabled successive one-year extensions of the ED and CBI Directors' tenures up to five years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sanjay Kumar Mishra was appointed ED Director in 2018 and received multiple extensions before the Supreme Court's July 2023 ruling.

 

• Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul later also headed benches in several significant constitutional matters before retiring from the Supreme Court in December 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• Justice KM Joseph, Justice Ajay Rastogi, Justice Mukesh Shah (Options 1, 2, 4): These judges were not the ones who recused themselves from this particular case; the recusal was specifically by Justice SK Kaul.
